upstream.role: edge worker (source authorization auditor) — READ-ONLY source pass
upstream.scope: supabase/functions/**, apps/**, packages/** — source text only
upstream.authority: SOURCE ONLY. Effective DB privileges, policy predicates, view security_invoker, RPC secdef/search_path and storage policy rows are the ACL worker catalog's to state. Policy/RLS columns here are HINTS and several are known-wrong because many policies are created inside `execute format(...)` loops (see unknowns.dynamicDdl).
upstream.method: Full read of all 22 function entrypoints + 17 _shared modules; scripted AST-free scan of every .from()/.rpc() in apps+packages with hand resolution of every dynamic table expression; grep of all 363 migrations for grant/policy/bucket text.

dbRoles.anon: Anonymous public endpoints (application-*, public-module-*) reach the DB only through service_role inside the function, so anon needs no table privilege for them.
dbRoles.authenticated: CRITICAL: both WORKS employees AND logged-in GUESTs run as this single Postgres role. The guest custom JWT carries role:"authenticated" (guestAccount.ts:328) and is signed with GUEST_JWT_SECRET, which crypto.ts:15 states must equal the project JWT secret. Therefore every GRANT ... TO authenticated is reachable by a guest session and is separated from employee data by RLS predicates alone.
dbRoles.service_role: Edge functions only. No browser path.

findings.severity: P0 (latent — no send path exists today)
findings.title: notifications-dispatch accepts an arbitrary recipient and an arbitrary credential-bearing template from any Supabase Auth user
findings.why: The template registry (_shared/notifications.ts:15-62) contains GUEST_OTP, GUEST_PASSWORD_RESET (with a caller-supplied {{link}}), and GUEST_INVITE_NEW (which instructs the reader to log in with their registered phone digits). Any holder of any employee session could therefore send an arbitrary address a message that renders as an official Y&Archer password-reset carrying an attacker-chosen URL, from the company's own verified sender.

findings.title: notifications-dispatch has zero callers anywhere and writes no audit record
findings.why: A generic, unauthenticated-in-practice send primitive that nothing uses is pure attack surface, and it would leave no trace if used.

findings.title: apps/guest calls an edge function that does not exist in the repo
findings.why: Either a deployed function exists with no source under version control — in which case its authorization is unreviewable and unreproducible from a clean replay — or the temporary-guest page is silently broken. Both need an answer before AUTHZ closes. This is a source-side observation; the deployed function list is not visible from here.

findings.title: Four functions resolve the caller without the is_active / external-role checks that internalAuth performs
findings.why: A deactivated employee whose Supabase Auth session is still alive passes these gates. Impact is bounded — the aiFill functions immediately re-ask canWrite/canCreate under the caller token, material-download re-queries rows under the caller token, and employee-create still requires super_admin or management write — so this is a defence-in-depth inconsistency, not an open door. But it means "deactivate the employee" is not by itself a complete revocation for these five paths; the RLS helper behind current_app_user_id() is what actually has to hold the line.

findings.title: CORS grace mode leaves 18 of 22 functions callable from any origin
findings.why: guest-auth-login, guest-auth-password, employee-create and material-download are all reachable cross-origin until the operations secret is set. The code already documents this as a pre-production requirement; it belongs on the deploy checklist, not in a code change.

findings.severity: P0 for the ACL decision (not an exposure)
findings.title: GUEST sessions and WORKS employees share the single `authenticated` Postgres role
findings.why: Every `grant ... to authenticated` the ACL worker writes is simultaneously a grant to logged-in external startups and experts. Nothing at the privilege layer separates them — only the RLS predicate does. Concretely, apps/guest reads program_announcements, program_modules, program_posts, program_links, program_notices, program_overviews, attachments and reads+inserts program_questions with that role. The finite grant set must be justified against the guest threat model, not only the employee one.

findings.title: One browser DELETE survives the soft-delete rule
findings.why: Either this is an approved exception (payment lines are a replace-set, re-inserted wholesale by set_capital_call_payments) and DELETE must be granted, or the client path is dead code that the RPC already superseded. `set_capital_call_payments` exists at fund/hooks.ts:427, which suggests the latter. Needs one look before the grant matrix is fixed.

findings.title: partner-docs bucket retains its row after its policies were dropped

non_findings: The three anonymous endpoints (public-module-get, public-module-file, application-form-get, application-submit) use service_role deliberately and are gated by a single unit-tested pure function (publicModuleLinkGate.ts, publicModuleLinkGate.test.ts). Bypassing RLS here is the design, not a defect — the gate is the authorization and each function narrows its own output.

guest-access-invite and guest-password-reset do NOT use service_role for the authorization decision; they delegate to SECURITY INVOKER RPCs under the caller token and only then escalate. This is the correct pattern and should not be flagged.

A SECURITY DEFINER function with public EXECUTE is not automatically a defect. The aiFill profiles depend on can_write_startup / can_create_startup / can_write_ma_seller / can_create_ma_seller / attachment_refs being callable by authenticated — that is the mechanism by which the edge function refuses to copy the permission predicate. Revoking EXECUTE on these would break the AI-fill authorization path, not harden it.
entity_contributions INSERT by authenticated is intentional and documented (docs_master/CLAUDE.md §3): the actor column is overwritten by a BEFORE INSERT trigger.

unknowns.note: Everything in tables[].grantInSource is migration TEXT, not catalog state. Legacy auto-exposed privileges from before auto_expose_new_tables was unset are invisible from source and are exactly what the ACL worker's replayed catalog must enumerate.

unknowns.dynamicDdl: Policies for at least these migrations are created inside `execute format(...)` loops and cannot be read by grep: 20260705150500_ac_rls, 20260705170000_fund_schema, 20260705180000_mna_schema, 20260705200000_project_schema, 20260705210000_management_schema, 20260803230100_program_module_content, 20260903100000_program_module_ledger_unify, 20260903110000_module_content_rls_polymorphic, 20260903120000_guest_portal_all_program_workspaces. A naive scan reports funds, investments, capital_calls, assets, kpi_records, dept_budgets, application_forms and application_submissions as having no policy; they do, via those loops. No policy conclusion should be drawn from this artifact.

unknowns.note: trade_partners_directory is a VIEW (20260903230000:32) already granted SELECT. app.network_entities_union is an app-schema view granted SELECT (20260731230000:77). kpi_results is granted but has no browser callsite. security_invoker settings are unverified here.
The 80 RPCs are listed as demand only. secdef / search_path / EXECUTE grants unverified from source.
guest-temp-resolve (E-3) cannot be resolved from the repo. Requires whoever can see the deployment.

supabase/config.toml has no [functions] section and no verify_jwt setting anywhere in the repo. Whether the platform pre-validates Authorization before the handler runs — and therefore whether the guest custom JWT and the anonymous endpoints behave as the code assumes — is a deployment fact this audit cannot establish.
Both carry grants in migration source but have zero browser callsites in this scan. Either RPC-only or dead. Candidates for revocation review.
